items.item_text: resume
cover letter
HR certification (SHRM-SCP, SPHR, or equivalent) (Preferred)
Advanced degree and/or comparable experience/training (Preferred)
Bachelor's degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, or related field and/or equivalent experience/training.
Demonstrated experience providing strategic HR consultation and leadership in a unionized environment, including interpreting and applying collective bargaining agreements.
Experience supporting skilled trades, facilities, operations, or similarly represented workforces in a strategic HR capacity.
Proven experience fostering inclusive and equitable workplace practices.

The Human Resources Director serves as a senior-level advisor and people strategist, responsible for shaping and implementing workforce and organizational strategies for Facilities Services by providing expert human resources consultation. This position provides consultative, strategic guidance and partners with internal and centralized teams to ensure effective execution of transactional services including recruitment, onboarding, employee and labor relations, classification and compensation, performance, and talent management.
Employee & Labor Relations Leadership - 35%

The Human Resources Director functions as a trusted partner to senior leadership, balancing strategic organizational development, workforce planning, and compliance with policy and best practice. This role applies expert knowledge of HR, organizational design and performance, and organizational behavior principles and practices to identify and address root causes of organizational challenges, helping leaders navigate complexity and translate strategic priorities into actionable, sustainable outcomes.

Advises leadership on sensitive employee and labor relations issues and proactively identifies patterns, risks, and opportunities to strengthen leadership effectiveness and organizational health while also ensuring consistency with UC policy, law, and applicable labor contracts.

This position serves as a point of integration with People & Culture (P&C) functions and Berkeley Regional Services (BRS) functions, ensuring coordinated, aligned delivery of HR services that reflect both institutional priorities and organizational needs. The Human Resources Director operates independently, exercising a high degree of judgment and strategic influence across complex HR domains.
Partners with Employee & Labor Relations, Legal, BRS and other partners to resolve complex issues.
Performs or supports staff in preliminary investigations
Coaches and trains managers in performance management, conflict resolution, and engagement strategies.
Ensures equitable and compliant HR practices that support a positive work environment.
Serves as a Skelly Officer, as needed, for campus-wide disciplinary matters
Team Leadership & Collaboration - 25%
Provides direct supervision, coaching, and performance management for HR staff
Operates as a connector across functions, leaders, other campus units, and priorities
Facilitates alignment across stakeholders to reduce fragmentation and ensure leaders experience HR services as coordinated, strategic, and effective.
Ensures clarity of roles, priorities, and accountability across the team to support consistent, high-quality service delivery.
Facilitates cross-unit HR coordination, best practice sharing, and professional development within the HR community.
Represents the department on campus-wide HR workgroups or strategic projects.
Promotes a collaborative, high-trust HR partnership model.
Strategic Consultation & Workforce Planning - 15%

Serves as a consultative, trusted advisor to leadership, facilitating alignment across units to ensure clarity, consistency, and effective operations by aligning people strategies with short- and long-term organizational priorities.

Assists unit Directors with workforce and succession planning efforts, analyzing organizational structure, capability gaps, and future workforce needs to inform proactive planning and decision-making.
Advises on reorganizations, new positions, reclassifications, change management, culture, and future workforce design.
Partners with managers to ensure compliance with campus policy.
Organizational Development & Culture - 15%
Coordinates departmental functions to ensure efforts are aligned, integrated, and effectively implemented to support desired organizational culture and performance outcomes.
Integrates engagement and belonging principles into workforce strategy and leadership development efforts.
Provides for the delivery, either directly or through others, of workshops and resources for managers to improve inclusive supervision and organizational effectiveness.
Compiles and uses workforce data and feedback to identify cultural or systemic improvement areas.
Program Leadership, Implementation & HR Operations - 10%
Supports complex, cross-functional initiatives addressing workforce transformation, organizational effectiveness, and culture change.
Exercises judgment in prioritizing initiatives and balancing client needs with institutional direction and available resources.
Leads departmental rollout of P&C programs and initiatives (e.g., performance management, policy updates, new and successor labor contract implementation, new systems).
Reviews HR processes for compliance and efficiency; identifies improvements to align with UC and divisional goals.
Ensures quality and consistency of HR service delivery and data integrity.
Demonstrated political acumen, discretion, and sound judgment in managing complex situations.
Demonstrated ability to foster and lead effective teams, supervise and manage staff.

Expert knowledge of HR concepts, policies, procedures, and ability to provide strategic consultation to senior leadership on culture, compensation, labor, employee relations, workforce planning, organizational design, reorganizations, change management, and workforce strategy.
Proven ability to advise senior leaders on complex employee and labor relations matters, including performance management, disciplinary matters, conflict resolution, and policy interpretation.
Ability to analyze workforce trends, organizational needs, and HR data to develop recommendations and inform leadership decision-making.
Demonstrated ability to consult with senior leaders and influence organizational direction.
Excellent analytical, problem-solving, and project management skills.
Strong interpersonal and communication skills; ability to build trust and credibility with diverse constituencies.
